Visit note | 2025-05-17 09:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Abdul Gazi, 43, male. Mr. Gazi returns for review, reporting that he still suffers from breathlessness during attacks and sudden bursts of a racing heart. He recalls that his first severe attack happened at a busy market in Shyamoli. He works as a construction worker and has been under heavy stress trying to support his family. He has Essential hypertension and has experienced about 9 panic attacks in the last month. He denies chest pain radiating to the jaw or arm and denies suicidal ideation. On examination: BP 143/95 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 48 kg. He appears anxious and tense. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-05-17 10:00 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Rahim Sikder, 72, male. Mr. Sikder attends for a follow-up assessment regarding his long history of smoking, wheezing on walking, and breathlessness that has been worse for several days. He mentions his symptoms flared after rubbish was burned near his home in Sirajganj. He describes himself as a homemaker around the house nowadays and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies chest pain or fever. On examination: SpO2 90%, BP 128/75 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 53 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheezes and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-05-17 10:00 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ayesha Alam, 19, female. Miss Alam comes in reporting loose watery stools and vomiting that began after a picnic in Motijheel. She works as a delivery rider and has no known comorbidities. Notably, she presents with high fever and blood in the stool with little vomiting. She reports crampy abdominal discomfort but no rigidity. On examination: pulse 114 bpm, BP 125/80 mmHg, weight 81 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild generalized tenderness. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink small sips of fluid often, eat bland foods like rice, bananas, and toast, and wash hands before eating. Follow-up in 2 days if the stools do not settle.

Visit note | 2025-05-17 10:30 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Rezaul Gazi, 20, male. Mr. Gazi presents for his first visit with a sudden high fever, severe aching in his bones and muscles, and a faint rash on his arms. He is an architect and notes his illness started after a week of stagnant rainwater around his house in Cox's Bazar. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies cough, sore throat, or dysuria. On examination: temperature 103.0°F, platelet count 128000 per microlitre, BP 132/83 mmHg, pulse 104 bpm, weight 78 kg. He appears flushed with mild conjunctival injection. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-05-17 10:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tariq Karim, 70, male. Mr. Karim presents for an initial consultation complaining of pain that wakes him at night, pain that eases after eating, and gnawing pain in his upper belly. He states this started after irregular meals on night shifts in Tongi. He works as a shopkeeper and has Essential hypertension. He denies vomiting blood or passing black tarry stools. On examination: pain score 7/10, BP 142/93 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 84 kg. Epigastric tenderness is present without guarding. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.
